objective: Restore reliable daily publication continuity in The Word while preserving the current BUKLOD devotional architecture and keeping production unchanged.
productionBaselineEvidence: verified: DEV source baseline is main at 11cf6bd096054dbf8ac204186b199fc835e740e3. Production artifact and live fingerprint were not changed or claimed as verified because this work is DEV-only.
chosenApproach: Correct the existing The Word query selection and lifecycle refresh, extract deterministic schedule/archive selection into a small pure helper, and add focused Node regression tests.
selectionRationale: The existing screen sorts daily publications oldest-first inside the current week and falls back to a previous week. Reusing the existing route and devotionals table fixes the behavior without schema, RLS, auth, or module redesign.
acceptanceChecks: The featured Word is the newest published date within the current Monday-start week and never falls back to an older week.
Earlier daily Words remain newest-first in the archive, with duplicate publication dates and future-dated cache entries excluded.
The screen refreshes on revisit, app foreground return, and local midnight without continuous background polling.
Existing membership gate, detail route, account-scoped offline cache, and Supabase security remain unchanged.
preserveBehaviors: Existing devotionals table and is_published/publish_date publication controls.
Monday-start week convention and current devotional detail route.
Cluster membership gate and account-scoped offline cache.
No production OTA, schema, RLS, authentication, or unrelated module changes.
alternativeApproaches: Create a new database view or RPC for daily Word selection; rejected because the issue is deterministic client-side selection and no schema change is needed.
Poll Supabase continuously in the background; rejected because it adds needless requests and battery/network cost.
Keep the current oldest-first weekly selection with a manual refresh; rejected because it leaves the stale featured Word defect unresolved.
